children: President Donald Trump is expected to host Anthropic

CEO Dario Amodei for a private dinner at the White House on Sunday, a meeting that could signal improving relations between the administration and one of the country’s leading artificial intelligence companies.

The dinner will mark the first one-on-one meeting between Trump and Amodei, Axios reported, citing people familiar with the plans. Trump personally invited Amodei after the Anthropic chief was unable to attend a White House state dinner last week because of a scheduling conflict.
The meeting comes ahead of a larger White House gathering Tuesday, when Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson are expected to meet with executives from several major AI companies.
Relations show signs of a thaw
and the Trump administration have had a turbulent relationship this year, with disagreements over AI safety, regulation and national security.

In June, Trump told Axios that he had recently viewed Anthropic as a potential national security threat, although he indicated at the time that tensions had begun to ease. The administration's treatment of the company had included export restrictions and a Pentagon designation of Anthropic as a supply-chain risk.

More recently, some Trump allies have criticized Amodei over his warnings about the potential dangers of advanced AI. A memo circulated within the White House last week sought to connect Amodei with the effective altruism movement and portrayed his approach to AI safety as being at odds with the administration's push to accelerate U.S. development of the technology. Anthropic has sought to distance itself from the effective altruism label.

Axios also reported Sunday that Amodei's critics were circulating another negative briefing about him ahead of the dinner. The document was not produced by the White House and its origins were unclear.

A direct meeting with Trump could give Anthropic (ANHTRO) an opportunity to improve its standing with an administration that is shaping U.S. policy on AI development, export controls and national security.
Anthropic is one of the major developers of frontier AI models and competes with OpenAI
and other technology companies for customers, computing resources and influence over emerging AI policy.

The dinner also comes as the White House places increasing emphasis on U.S. leadership in advanced AI. A White House official told Axios that the administration wants the U.S. to lead in superintelligence while protecting consumers and maintaining American competitiveness.

, better relations with Trump could become particularly important as Washington makes decisions that could affect how AI companies develop their models, sell their technology to the government and compete internationally.
